name: Skobeloff Green
lede: Skobeloff Green is a saturated teal catalogued by Ridgway in 1912 and again by Maerz and Paul in 1930, and no book we hold explains who or what Skobeloff was.

sections.title: A name the books leave open
sections.body:
Ridgway placed this teal on plate VII of his 1912 *Color Standards and Color Nomenclature*, hue 39 [1]. Maerz and Paul's 1930 dictionary repeats it on their plate 25, dated to 1912, the same year as Ridgway's book [1]. The ISCC-NBS system of 1955 files it as block 160 [1]. No book we hold records who or what Skobeloff was [2].

Its nearest library neighbor is [[dark-cyan|Dark Cyan]], about 3.2 units away, with the brighter [[mint-turquoise|Mint Turquoise]] close behind [3].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Measured in LCH terms it is strongly saturated, lightness 52, chroma 33, hue 188 degrees, close to [[teal]] but greener, and not far from the darker [[arsenate]] [3]. Our archive of 23,781 paintings, as photographed, finds only 2 matches, both twentieth-century: Odilon Redon's 1895 *Sommeil de Caliban* and a 1924 still life by Patrick Henry Bruce [4]. Such a saturated teal rarely survives as photographed on aged, varnished canvases [4].
